requirement:
Each documented profile defines which grammar nodes are comments; the Markdown
profile's comments are HTML comment blocks, so an inline HTML comment within a
paragraph remains ordinary paragraph text. In every supported language, comments on consecutive lines with no other source
between them MUST form one comment run. A comment that follows other source on
the same line, including another comment, MUST form a run by itself and MUST belong to the innermost outline node
containing that line. Any other run MUST belong to the next outline node that
starts after it within the smallest node containing it; when that container has
no such node, the run MUST belong to the container, which is the root node at top
level. A profile MAY bind a comment kind to its container
instead: such a run MUST belong to the smallest node containing it. The Rust
profile MUST bind inner doc comments (`//!`, `/*!`) to their container, so a
file-level inner doc comment belongs to the root node. Habeas MUST retain the
one-based line and UTF-8 byte column of each inline role’s opening brace or
fenced reference’s first opening colon. When siblings share a line, the
reference belongs to the item owning the comment at that position. A reference
in a comment MUST count for the node its run belongs to under
{cite}`requirements.references.coverage.tests` and
{cite}`requirements.references.authoring_inputs`.
rationale:
structural: `requirements.references.outline_comments` has no implementation roots, and none are needed. Every clause states observable behavior, so none creates a structural obligation.

- **Comment runs.** Consecutive-line comments MUST form one run. A comment that follows other source on its line MUST form a run by itself. Both rules fix how comments are grouped. An implementation could group them with any algorithm or data structure and give the same results.
- **Run ownership.** A run belongs to the innermost containing node, to the next node that starts after it, or to its container. A profile MAY bind a comment kind to its container instead. The Rust profile MUST bind inner doc comments (`//!`, `/*!`) to their container. These clauses say which outline node a reference counts for. They do not say how to build the outline or which interface to use. Any implementation that assigns the same node satisfies them.
- **Profile definitions.** "Each documented profile defines which grammar nodes are comments" describes the documented profile behavior. It does not prescribe a library, type or signature. The Markdown rule that HTML comment blocks are comments and inline HTML comments are paragraph text is also behavior.
- **Position retention.** "Habeas MUST retain the one-based line and UTF-8 byte column" is the closest candidate to a structural obligation. An implementation could store the position in a field, or recompute it from the source on demand. Either way the observable positions and attribution are identical, so the storage choice is discretionary. The text names no field, type or interface for it.
- **Counting references.** "A reference in a comment MUST count for the node its run belongs to" under `requirements.references.coverage.tests` and `requirements.references.authoring_inputs` is observable behavior of those requirements. The requirement cites them for context only. It does not prescribe how they delegate to this one.

The requirement has `Tests` edges and no `Implements` edges. That fits a behavior-only requirement whose evidence is tests. No structural gap needs a marker.

behavioral: I found no test-adequacy gap. Each obligation in `requirements.references.outline_comments` maps to a test that exercises it and asserts the outcome.

- **Profile-defined comments and Markdown.**
  - `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/tests.rs#fn[markdown_comments_are_html_comment_blocks_not_inline_comments]` asserts that only the block comment is a comment. It also asserts that the inline `<!-- -->` stays paragraph text.
  - `fn[comment_runs_follow_the_same_rules_in_every_language]` covers every documented profile: Rust (elsewhere), Python, TypeScript, TSX, CSS, TOML, YAML and Markdown. A search of the profile table (`fn[every_profile_mapping_is_documented]`) shows these are the only profiles.
- **Consecutive-line comments form one run.**
  - `fn[comment_between_two_fns_belongs_to_the_next]` and `fn[comment_runs_belong_to_the_next_node_or_their_container]` cover multi-line runs separated by blank lines.
  - `src/fenced.rs#mod[tests]/fn[comment_fences_close_within_one_comment_run]` checks that a fence cannot close across a blank-line gap.
  - `fn[distinct_runs_with_the_same_owner_do_not_close_each_others_fences]` checks that an inner-doc change or a trailing opener ends a run.
- **A comment after other source on its line.**
  - It forms its own run and belongs to the innermost node containing that line. This is covered by `fn[comment_after_code_on_a_line_belongs_to_that_lines_node]`, which includes a comment after a closing brace.
  - A comment after another comment is covered by `fn[a_comment_after_another_comment_on_its_line_forms_its_own_run]`. The first comment goes to `fn[b]`; the second goes to the root.
  - The trailing-comment cases in the multi-language test cover the other languages.
- **Any other run.**
  - A run belongs to the next node that starts after it within the smallest containing node. If there is none, it belongs to the container, which is the root at top level. Coverage:
    - next node: `fn[comment_runs_belong_to_the_next_node_or_their_container]`;
    - container when nothing follows: `fn[trailing_comment_after_last_fn_in_mod_belongs_to_the_mod]` and `fn[top_level_comment_with_nothing_after_belongs_to_the_root]`;
    - YAML: `fn[yaml_comments_before_a_key_belong_to_that_key_not_the_previous_one]`.
- **Rust inner doc comments bind to the container.** `fn[file_level_inner_doc_comments_and_unmapped_code_belong_to_the_root]` covers `//!` and `/*!` at file level. `fn[comment_runs_belong_to_the_next_node_or_their_container]` covers `//!` inside `mod m`, which belongs to `mod[m]`.
- **Line and UTF-8 byte column, and siblings sharing a line.** `src/inputs.rs#mod[tests]/fn[references_in_sibling_comments_on_one_line_use_their_byte_columns]` uses `Café` and CRLF so that byte and char columns differ.
  - It asserts a one-based line and byte column for both an inline `{impl}` and a fenced `:::`.
  - It asserts that each reference's owner is its own sibling (`Café` and `Two`).
  - `fn[yaml_evidence_ranges_follow_comment_ownership_between_sibling_entries]` and `fn[evidence_preserves_attachment_lines_and_declaration_positions]` add further position and ownership checks.
- **A comment reference counts for its run's owner.**
  - Under `requirements.references.coverage.tests`, `src/rust_coverage.rs#mod[tests]/fn[test_functions_need_a_test_reference]` covers an attached comment, a body comment, closed and unclosed fences, and cite-only or impl-only references.
  - Under `requirements.references.authoring_inputs`, `src/authoring/inputs.rs#mod[tests]/fn[references_contribute_their_owning_outline_nodes]` and `fn[direct_test_edges_select_the_nested_item_without_expanding_its_citations]` check that the owning outline node is contributed.

The optional "profile MAY bind a comment kind" clause imposes nothing to check beyond the Rust inner-doc rule above.

:::{req} coverage.tests
Every Rust function carrying a test attribute, `#[test]` or an attribute whose
path ends in `test` such as `#[tokio::test]`, including those in Cargo
integration-test targets, MUST carry a `{test}` reference to a requirement or
named example under {cite}`requirements.references.roles`, in a comment
attached to it or within its body. A test function without one MUST be a
validation error naming its file, line, and name.
:::{req} authoring_inputs
When authoring evidence, the edges defined by
{cite}`requirements.references.roles` MUST determine the reference
contributions to the mandatory input set defined by
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`. A `{cite}` made by the subject
MUST contribute the cited definition's complete fenced declaration. A requirement
or example declaration that references the subject with `{impl}` or `{test}`
MUST contribute that complete declaration. For sources outside such declarations,
an `{impl}` reference or `:impl:` anchor alone MUST NOT contribute source text,
except for structural assessments under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.structural_inputs`;
those sources MUST remain discoverable under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.reference_index` and MAY be requested under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.source_tools`. Sources with only `{cite}` edges into the subject
MUST NOT contribute and MUST remain discoverable under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.reference_index`. A `:test:` anchor under
{cite}`requirements.references.anchors` MUST contribute the complete anchored file,
or for a `path#selector` anchor the anchored node.
An in-source `{test}` reference to the subject MUST contribute the source
containing it: for a reference in a supported language, the smallest enclosing
outline node under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`; for a reference in a Markdown requirement, example, or
terminology declaration, that complete declaration; for other references, the
complete containing source file. Literal references, evidence copies, and
generated output MUST remain excluded under the existing reference-discovery
rules.
An in-source `{fixme}` reference alone MUST NOT contribute the containing source
to the mandatory input set. Its acknowledgment MUST instead be supplied under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.fixme_inputs`.
These contribution rules MUST apply only to the assessed subject's direct
references. Including another declaration or source MUST NOT by itself recursively
expand that source's own edges. Reference links MUST NOT be described as proof
that all substantively relevant sources have been found.
